label: Transportation
assignment: Discover realistic transportation resources for people in {service_area} who cannot reliably reach work, health care, food, benefits, education, or other essential services. Follow transit agencies and coordinating organizations to specific fixed-route, paratransit, medical, voucher, volunteer-driver, vehicle, bicycle, and emergency-ride programs. Verify trip purpose, eligibility, coverage, hours, fare, reservation, accessibility, and pickup reliability.
include: Fixed-route transit, reduced fares, passes, route planning, and first-mile or last-mile links
ADA paratransit, senior, disability, and door-to-door transportation
Non-emergency medical transport, Medicaid rides, hospital and treatment transportation
Ride vouchers, volunteer drivers, employment rides, vehicle repair, donated vehicles, bicycles, and licenses
Rural coverage, advance reservations, companions, mobility devices, language, and urgent-trip realities
exclude: Ordinary taxi or rideshare options without a subsidy or accessible hardship pathway
Transit information that does not establish whether the needed origin, destination, and time are served
Vehicle donation pages that solicit vehicles but do not place transportation with clients
verificationQuestions: Which trip purposes, origins, destinations, days, and hours are covered?
What eligibility certification, reservation notice, fare, and cancellation policy applies?
Are wheelchairs, mobility devices, attendants, children, and language needs accommodated?
How reliable is pickup, and what option exists for urgent or recurring trips?

stages.title: Public transit and reduced fares
stages.instruction: Investigate fixed routes, on-demand zones, reduced fares and passes, route planning, first-mile and last-mile connections, service hours, and practical links to essential destinations.

stages.title: Paratransit and essential trips
stages.instruction: Investigate ADA paratransit, senior and disability rides, Medicaid and medical transport, treatment and veteran transportation, certification, reservations, fares, attendants, and mobility-device access.

stages.title: Vouchers and transportation stability
stages.instruction: Investigate ride vouchers, volunteer drivers, employment transport, vehicle repair or placement, bicycles, driver licensing, fuel help, and safe alternatives when public transit does not fit.

stages.title: Coverage and reliability review
stages.instruction: Test origins, destinations, early and late hours, weekends, rural areas, reservation windows, accessibility, child travel, urgent trips, and recurring needs. Exclude unsubsidized commercial rides and donation-only programs.
